harmonicFunction: D (I) - Strong tonic center in D major throughout the song
Cadd9 (bVII) - Flattened seventh with added 9th for color in the intro
G (IV) - Subdominant providing warm harmonic resolution
A (V) - Dominant creating forward momentum in verse and chorus
Am (v) - Minor dominant used in the guitar interlude for darker color
G/B - Slash chord creating smooth bass line movement in the intro

techniques.name: Arpeggiated Chord Picking
techniques.description: The iconic fingerpicked/hybrid-picked intro using open chord voicings with sustained bass notes and arpeggiated patterns that define the song's identity

notes: D chord: X-X-0-2-3-2 with arpeggiated picking across strings
Dsus4: X-X-0-2-3-3 adding the sus4 embellishment
Cadd9: X-3-2-0-3-0 open voicing with the added 9th
G/B: X-2-0-0-3-3 providing the descending bass line
Each chord is picked string by string, not strummed
Let notes ring into each other for a shimmering effect
sequence: Pick the bass note of each chord first with the thumb or pick
Arpeggiate upward through the chord tones on higher strings
Allow strings to ring openly for maximum sustain
Transition to the next chord while letting the previous notes decay
tips: Use a clean guitar tone with slight chorus for the intro arpeggio
Practice each chord change slowly to ensure smooth bass note transitions
Focus on even timing between each picked note in the arpeggio
A hybrid picking approach (pick + fingers) can make the pattern easier
details.progression: D - Dsus4 - D - Cadd9 - G/B - G

techniques.name: Power Chord Rhythm with Dynamic Shifts
techniques.description: Transitions from the clean arpeggiated intro to full distorted power chord rhythm, creating the signature clean-to-distorted dynamic that defines the song's arrangement

notes: D5: X-5-7-7-X-X or open D power chord voicing
A5: X-0-2-2-X-X (open A string power chord)
G5: 3-5-5-X-X-X (barre power chord)
The verse and chorus shift to full power chord strumming
Heavy sustain and compression characterize the distorted sections
sequence: Begin with clean arpeggiated intro tone
Switch to distorted/overdriven channel for the verse entry
Use strong downstrokes for power chord rhythm sections
Maintain consistent strumming power through verse and chorus
tips: The transition from clean to distorted must be seamless - practice the switch
Tom Scholz used heavy compression for sustain - simulate with a compressor pedal
Power chords should ring fully without excessive palm muting
Match the energy increase from clean intro to full band sections
details.progression: D - A - G verse / G - A - D chorus

techniques.name: Harmonized Lead Guitar
techniques.description: Dual harmonized guitar leads using major thirds and octaves, a signature Tom Scholz technique that creates the layered Boston guitar sound

notes: Lead lines are harmonized in thirds (two guitars playing the same melody a third apart)
Uses D major scale for the harmonized passages
The guitar interlude section features the most prominent harmonized leads
Requires precise intonation from both guitar parts to sound correct
sequence: Learn the primary melody line in D major pentatonic
Learn the harmony part a third above the primary melody
Practice each part separately before combining
Use delay and reverb to create the layered studio sound
tips: If playing solo, focus on the primary melody line first
Use a looper pedal to practice both parts together
Heavy sustain and compression are key to replicating the Scholz tone
Precision is more important than speed in harmonized parts
details.progression: Am - G - D harmonized guitar section

sections.name: Intro (Arpeggiated)
sections.description: The iconic clean arpeggiated intro that is one of rock's most recognizable and beloved guitar openings, featuring open chord voicings with a descending bass line
sections.progression: D - Dsus4 - D - Cadd9 - G/B - G
notes: Clean guitar tone with subtle chorus effect
Each note should ring clearly into the next
Descending bass line D - C - B - G creates smooth movement
This intro is played on acoustic or clean electric guitar

sections.name: Verse
sections.technique: Power Chord Rhythm with Dynamic Shifts
sections.description: Verse section where the full band enters with distorted power chords, creating a dramatic dynamic shift from the clean intro
notes: Full band enters with distorted guitar tone
Strong downstroke rhythm on power chords
Dramatic dynamic increase from the clean intro
Sustain on each chord for the classic Boston fullness

sections.name: Chorus
sections.technique: Power Chord Rhythm with Dynamic Shifts
sections.description: Anthemic chorus section with the IV-V-I progression driving the uplifting the signature vocal hook
sections.progression: G - A - D - G - A - D
notes: Maximum energy with full chord strumming
IV-V-I progression creates the uplifting, anthemic feel
Let chords ring with full sustain for the arena rock sound
Vocal hook the iconic vocal hook is the emotional peak

sections.name: Guitar Interlude
sections.description: The harmonized dual-guitar lead section that showcases Tom Scholz's signature layered guitar approach with thirds harmony
sections.progression: Am - G - D - Am - G - D
notes: Two guitars playing the same melody harmonized in thirds
Heavy sustain and compression for the classic Boston lead tone
Melody is built from D major pentatonic scale patterns
This section is a defining moment of the song and the Boston sound

sections.name: Outro
sections.description: Returns to the arpeggiated intro pattern over the final chorus, creating a bookend effect as the song builds to its conclusion
sections.progression: D - Dsus4 - D - Cadd9 - G/B - G (with full band)
notes: Return of the arpeggiated intro figure over the full band arrangement
Vocal ad-libs over the combined arpeggio and band texture
Builds to final climax before resolving
Fade-out ending with the arpeggio pattern repeating

beginner.title: Getting Started with More Than a Feeling
steps: Learn open D, C, G, Am, and A chord shapes
Practice basic arpeggiated picking across chord strings
Work on clean chord transitions at slow tempo
Master the Dsus4 embellishment on the D chord

intermediate.title: Mastering the Arpeggio and Power Chords
steps: Play the complete arpeggiated intro at tempo (110 BPM)
Practice the clean-to-distorted transition for the verse entry
Learn power chord rhythm sections with proper dynamics
Work on chorus chord progression with full strumming energy

advanced.title: Harmonized Leads and Complete Performance
steps: Learn the harmonized guitar lead melody lines
Develop the compressed, sustained lead tone
Master dynamic shifts across all song sections
Perform the complete song with authentic tone and arrangement

commonMistakes: Rushing the arpeggiated intro - maintain even spacing between picked notes
Not letting notes ring sufficiently during the intro chord arpeggios
Sloppy transitions from the clean intro to the distorted verse sections
Under-sustaining power chords - the Boston sound requires long, full chord sustain
practiceRoutine: Warm up with D major scale arpeggios across open chord shapes
Practice the intro arpeggio pattern slowly with a metronome at 80 BPM
Work on clean-to-distorted channel switching with smooth transitions
Practice the harmonized lead melody at half speed before full tempo
Play along with the original recording for tone and dynamic reference
focusAreas: Clean arpeggiated picking with even note spacing and sustain
Dynamic control between clean intro and distorted sections
Power chord rhythm consistency and fullness
Harmonized lead guitar accuracy and intonation
metronomeWork: Start the arpeggiated intro at 80 BPM with quarter-note clicks
Gradually increase to 110 BPM while keeping notes even and ringing
Practice power chord sections with eighth-note subdivision clicks
Work on the harmonized lead section at half tempo before full speed
